spoken: [hook] Reading about your goal feels like doing it. It isn't. || Why do we stop doing things we know are good for us? Reason twenty-four. || [turn] Say you want to write a book. Three books on writing, forty videos. || Pages written: zero. But it feels like weeks of work. || Learning feels like progress. You're busy, and it's all about the goal. But nothing gets made. || Then one day you see how far you haven't come. You quit. || So flip the order. Make first, learn second. || Write a hundred words, then watch one video. Run fifteen minutes, then read about form. || [land] Six weeks later: four thousand words, not forty videos. || Send this to the friend with a full bookmarks folder and an empty page. || [outro] That's what Deem-yor is for. Archive your dream today, and break it into small steps you can actually do. || [outro] Follow for one reason a day. Next: why you stop improving after month one. || [outro] What are you reading about instead of doing? The link's in the bio.

params.title: Why you stop improving after month one

caption.instagram:
How to stop procrastinating by learning: make first, learn second.

Why we stop doing things we know are good for us, reason #24: reading about it. Three books on writing, forty videos, zero pages. Learning feels like progress because you're busy and it's all about the goal. But nothing gets made, and one day you see how far you haven't come.

The fix:
- Make one thing first (100 words, a 15-minute run)
- Then learn one thing
- Only what today's step needs

What are you reading about instead of doing? Tell me below.
